metadata.proof: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: The user pk from the URL and POST body. The admin_user_edit view (line 483) loads any User by pk and instantiates UserAdminForm which includes the 'role' field (forms.py line 49). There is no check preventing request.user == user before allowing a role change. SINK: `form.save()` at line 487 persists the role change. Compare with admin_user_toggle (line 499) which explicitly checks `if user == request.user` and blocks self-disable. No equivalent guard exists for role changes — a FIRM_ADMIN can downgrade themselves to CLIENT, losing all admin access with no recovery path except another admin or database intervention.

extra.message: User Enumeration — registration form reveals existing usernames via unique-constraint validation error

metadata.proof: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: request.POST['username'] from the registration form. The RegistrationForm extends Django's UserCreationForm (forms.py line 28), which inherits username uniqueness validation from the User model's unique=True constraint. SINK: When `form.is_valid()` fails due to a duplicate username, Django renders the form with an error message like 'A user with that username already exists.' This is returned in the HTTP response (line 68), allowing an attacker to enumerate valid usernames by submitting registrations and observing error responses.

extra.message: CSV Import validates uploads by file extension only

metadata.proof: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: CSV import form accepts a file upload entirely under attacker control. `ImportForm.clean_csv_file` decides whether a file is a CSV solely by checking the client-controlled filename extension. SINK: A user can rename any file to .csv (or set a text/csv Content-Type) and the server will parse its contents as CSV rows via csv.DictReader. There is no MIME-type sniffing, magic-byte verification, or content-structure validation to confirm the file is actually a CSV.

extra.message: Unbounded CSV export rows allow memory/CPU exhaustion

metadata.citation:
matters = accessible_matters(request.user)
...
for m in matters:
    writer.writerow([...])
metadata.proof: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: `export_csv` iterates over every matter, deadline, and document accessible to the user and writes them all into the response with no LIMIT, pagination, or row cap. SINK: A FIRM_ADMIN (or any staff user with access to many matters) can request a huge export that consumes unbounded server memory and CPU while building the response. There is no pagination, LIMIT clause, or maximum-row check on any of the three export paths (matters, deadlines, documents).

extra.message: Disabling a user does not revoke API keys or sessions

metadata.proof: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: admin_user_toggle flips `user.is_active` but never deactivates the user's ApiKey records (`ApiKey.active` remains True) and does not flush their sessions. SINK: While ActiveUserMiddleware would log out a browser session on the next request, any active API key remains valid and usable. Combined with the api_matter_status endpoint (line 566) which only checks `ApiKey.active=True` and not `user.is_active`, a disabled user can continue calling the API and accessing matter data.

extra.message: API matter-status endpoint accepts keys belonging to disabled users

metadata.proof: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: X-API-Key header from the HTTP request. The API status lookup only verifies `ApiKey.active`; it does not filter on `key.user.is_active` or `key.user.disabled_at`. SINK: If an admin disables the key's owner (via admin_user_toggle without deactivating the key), the key still passes the `active=True` filter and `can_access_matter(key.user, matter)` is evaluated. The disabled user gains continued API access to matter status data despite being explicitly deactivated.

extra.message: DocumentEditForm mass-assigns visibility field permitting unauthorized document exposure

metadata.proof: DocumentEditForm.Meta.fields includes visibility. In document_update (cases/views.py:265), any user with can_modify_matter (i.e., assigned attorney or paralegal) can POST a new visibility value — including PUBLIC_FILING or CLIENT_SHARED — via the ModelForm. The view saves the form directly (form.save()) without validating the transition. This lets a staff member downgrade a privileged/internal document to client-visible, bypassing the confidentiality that visibility choices were designed to enforce. The audit log only records the change after the fact.

extra.message: Uploaded documents stored on disk without encryption at rest

metadata.proof: DocumentVersion.file is a standard Django FileField writing to MEDIA_ROOT (default local filesystem). The upload_path helper writes files under uploads/matter_{id}/doc_{id}/. The application stores sensitive legal documents (pleadings, evidence, contracts, privileged material) in cleartext. A disk-level compromise, backup exposure, or any user with filesystem access can read all uploaded matter documents. No encryption-at-rest layer is applied.

extra.message: Task assignment notifies staff outside the matter, leaking matter information

metadata.proof: The task_edit view (line 315) sets the assignee queryset to ALL attorneys and paralegals in the system, not filtered to users associated with the matter. If a form POST assigns the task to an attorney/paralegal who is not on the matter, line 322 creates a Notification with the task title (which may contain case details) and a link to the matter. That notification is visible to the assignee even though they are not authorized to access the matter, disclosing sensitive matter information (matter existence, title, and a navigable link).
